# Requirement Document Instructions

For requirement documents, use precise product language and avoid implementation details unless they affect scope, feasibility, risk, data, security, integration, or acceptance criteria.

Every requirement document must include:

- Status
- Source Raw Input
- Problem Statement
- Goals
- Non-Goals
- Personas and Stakeholders
- User Journeys
- Functional Requirements
- Non-Functional Requirements
- Data and Integration Requirements
- UX and Accessibility Requirements
- Security, Privacy, Compliance
- Analytics and Observability
- Rollout and Migration
- Acceptance Criteria
- Assumptions
- Risks and Mitigations
- Open Questions
- Traceability Matrix
- Freeze Checklist

Enterprise requirement documents should use the numbered structure in `templates/enterprise/enterprise-requirement-document.md` when the user requests enterprise, client, production-grade, or freeze-ready requirement work.

Acceptance criteria must be observable, testable, and tied to requirement IDs.
